generator.program.note: The program the authors chose to grow this taxon's vine species (named in each species' spec until G2.3a moved it here).

traits.division_pattern.note: APweb, Apiales page, Araliaceae (read 2026-10-16): Aralioideae pinnately to palmately compound. 'usually palmate' is our weighting (Schefflera s.l., Oreopanax, Hedera and Hydrocotyle palmate or palmately lobed; Polyscias, Aralia pinnate).

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431, 435: 5, rarely 3 to 12, petals.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431, 435: stamens 5 to 10, rarely 3 to many; Floral Diagrams p. 340 gives up to 120.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431, 435: carpels 2 to 5, rarely to many; Floral Diagrams p. 340 general formula 1 to 10, up to 200.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431: petals free (rarely basally joined or a cap), valvate. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431, 505: flowers epigynous, rarely hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 47 Araliaceae: mostly woody, some climbing by aerial roots (ivy); leaves alternate, rarely opposite; stipules joined to the leaf stalk's base or within it, rarely absent; flowers regular, in umbels, racemes or heads; calyx small on an inferior ovary; petals often 5; fruit a berry or drupe.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Araliaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Araliaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431, family Araliaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral (rarely opposite or whorled), usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_division.note: DELTA Araliaceae (read 2026-10-17; old circumscription, ~700 spp, 49 genera, Hydrocotyle excluded) codes leaves as mostly simple, often dissected, otherwise ternate, pinnate, palmate or decompound; its ranking counts genera, not species. Weighted by species (approximate modern sizes, not read this session): palmately compound Schefflera s.l. with Heptapleurum and Didymopanax (~600), pinnate Polyscias (~160), Aralia (~70), Eleutherococcus and Panax outweigh simple-leaved Hydrocotyle (~150), Oreopanax (mostly simple, ~150), Dendropanax (~90), Hedera, Fatsia, Trevesia. DELTA's genus-based 'mostly simple' conflicts, so medium. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.flowering_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431, family Araliaceae: flowering position terminal, usually; read as {"terminal": "usually"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add schizocarp (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 431: drupe, berry or schizocarp.
